plainFields.description: Last modification timestamp. Used for sync and audit trails, not null. Updated on any change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp - For retention/audit. If not null, channel is considered deleted. Satisfies compliance requirement for data retention/auditability.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_sections
models.description: Section Entity - Implements extensible, dynamic business section management, mapping to a requirement for modular dynamic site/app composition. Each entry defines a logical section/component within a given channel context (e.g., home banner, product carousel, promo area). Maintains strict 3NF by referencing both channels and storing only section configuration here; layout/data references in auxiliary tables/materialized views if needed. Example: onboarding an app 'Main Banner' section for 'mobile' channel. Key relationships: references ai_mall_backend_channels; may be referenced by content/config tables elsewhere. Special behaviors: Can be dynamically enabled/disabled or scheduled, but schedules are not stored here.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: channel_id
foreignFields.description: Related channel's {@link ai_mall_backend_channels.id}; identifies which channel this section belongs to, ensuring no cross-channel confusion.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Section code (domain-unique slug) - Used for programmatic reference. E.g., "main_banner", "featured_products". Meets normalization requirement: display name, config are not duplicated here.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Display name for the section (for admin/UIs), e.g., "Main Banner". Atomic, not null. Used for search/UI, separated from configuration content.

plainFields.name: enabled
plainFields.description: Logical activation flag for business scheduling. Required by dynamic rendering rules for channel UX composition. Must remain atomic; scheduling logic is externalized.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp for the section. Implements audit trail requirement. Not null.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Change timestamp; always updated on row update. Not null. Used in auxiliary processing and audit logging.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-deletion timestamp; null if not deleted, value set when removed for audit/compliance. Enforces audit/history policy.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_configurations
models.description: Configuration Entity - Satisfies the requirements for a centralized configuration registry (feature toggles, branded settings, etc.). Each row specifies a single atomic configuration item, maintaining 3NF and not duplicating setting values. For instance, feature toggles, limits, branding variables, API keys (encrypted elsewhere). Relationships: references channel and optional section for scope; config values are always atomic. Usage example: enabling a feature in a specific section of the web channel. Special behaviors: Only stores atomic key-value data. Aggregates or computed/pre-resolved settings are handled in views/external caches.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: channel_id
foreignFields.description: Configured channel's {@link ai_mall_backend_channels.id}. Null if config is system-global. Maintains 2NF: channel-specific overrides do not duplicate global config data.

foreignFields.name: section_id
foreignFields.description: Configured section's {@link ai_mall_backend_sections.id}. Null if config is for entire channel.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Config item name (machine-readable); enforced unique within channel/section scope. Normalized; avoids redundancy vs. human description. E.g., "max_recommended_items", "brand_accent_color".

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Config value (atomic). Storing as string makes it flexible for all config types. Atomic value by design—complex/aggregated representations handled outside core table. Example: "10", "#F47623", or JSON-encoded value. Enforces normalization: no multi-setting/storage.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Description or business comment - For admin clarity and auditability. For example, "Controls max items on home banner". Not used in production logic, only as meta.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp - Satisfies audit/logging and change traceability.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Modification timestamp; updated on any change. Implements audit trail requirement; not null.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-deletion timestamp, null if still active. Enforces compliance/audit/max retention. Satisfies business policy for configuration sunset/reversion.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_api_gateways
models.description: API Gateway Entity - Implements registry of API gateway endpoints, configs, and associations (see Architecture requirements for API gateway concept). Each record defines an API endpoint, domain mapping, and metadata for routing/auth. Strict normalization—one entry per gateway/route, no calculated fields. For example, registering "api.mall.com/v2" as the main API route for the 'web' channel. Key relationships: references channel (for business context); referenced by tenant or system audit if required. Special behaviors: Gateway can be temporarily suspended/enabled, and settings beyond route are handled externally.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: channel_id
foreignFields.description: Target channel's {@link ai_mall_backend_channels.id}; ensures requests are mapped to the correct business context.

plainFields.name: route_base
plainFields.description: Base route for this gateway (e.g., "/api/v1", "/mobile/"). Implements requirement for explicit, unambiguous routing. Atomic. No computed path fields stored here.

plainFields.name: domain
plainFields.description: Mapped domain for this gateway (FQDN or subdomain, e.g., "api.mall.com"). Per domain mapping, not null. No wildcard; each gateway registered separately. Used in endpoint discovery.

plainFields.name: enabled
plainFields.description: Gateway activation flag—allows quick suspension/reactivation. Only unaggregated atomic flag here.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Gateway creation time (audit/logs).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last config update timestamp (audit/tracking). Always required per system audit rules.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete timestamp if gateway route is removed. Null means active. Complies with retention, audit policies.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_tenants
models.description: Tenant Entity - Implements the business requirement for full multi-tenancy isolation, as described in system architecture and compliance documents. Each row defines a distinct brand, sub-platform, or logical business tenant (e.g., for white-labeling, brand separation, regional variants). Design: strictly 3NF; all channel, user, and config references use tenant_id rather than duplicating brand/business info. For example, onboarding a new brand/partner, all data is tied to a unique tenant. Key relationships: referenced by channels, users, configurations, etc. Special behaviors: Tenant may be archived, not deleted, to maintain historical integrity.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Tenant code (unique per instance) - e.g., "main_mall", "brandA", "partner2". Used for programmatic routing and scoping. Normalized: display name/config not duplicated here.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Display/business name of tenant (for admin/partner reference). Not null, atomic, normalized.

plainFields.name: archived
plainFields.description: Tenant archival flag—used for compliance, never hard-deletes. Implements regulatory retention. Example: true if tenant/brand offboarded.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this tenant/brand was onboarded. Used for onboarding processes, billing, audit.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last updated time; always atomic, not null, per audit policy.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_customers
models.description: Customer actor entity - Implements requirements from the User Management and Role Definition documents, for tracking registered shoppers and their operational context. This model supports customer account onboarding, profile linkage, role enforcement (customer-only scope), and privacy compliance. Maintains 3NF by separating identity, credential, and role logic. For example, a typical customer uses this record as the root for shopping history, favorites, and personalization. Key relationships: main profile (user_profiles), credentials, roles. Special behaviors: deactivated or GDPR-erased accounts are soft-deleted but maintain audit trail.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each customer record.

foreignFields.name: user_profile_id
foreignFields.description: Associated user profile's {@link ai_mall_backend_user_profiles.id}. Connects this customer to their profile data for extensibility, privacy, and normalization.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Customer's normalized, login/account email address - Implements authentication and notification requirements. Ensures account uniqueness and for privacy/audit linkage. Example: 'alice@customer.com'.

plainFields.name: phone_number
plainFields.description: Customer's primary contact phone - Implements phone-based auth/contact. Used for notifications and 2FA flows if enabled. Example: '+821012345678'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp for audit and lifecycle tracking. Ensures event traceability and compliance with audit/retention requirements. Example: '2025-07-01T10:00:00Z'.

plainFields.name: deactivated_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for account deactivation or privacy erasure. Ensures compliance with right-to-be-forgotten and lifecycle rules. Nullable, only present when account is deactivated.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_sellers
models.description: Seller actor entity - Implements requirements for third-party vendors/partners as outlined in Role Definition and User Management modules. Maintains 3NF by isolating seller identity, profile, and access credentials. Used for product listing, order fulfillment, and analytics scoping. Example use: seller links to their shop's catalog and is constrained to their own data. Key relationships: main profile, credentials, roles. Special: Profile and role links ensure extensibility, audit, and privacy compliance.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for seller entity.

foreignFields.name: user_profile_id
foreignFields.description: Associated user profile's {@link ai_mall_backend_user_profiles.id}. Seller-specific profile/data linkage, keeping schema normalized and extensible.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Seller's unique business email for authentication/notification. Enforces account uniqueness and enables seller communications. Example: 'vendor@shop.com'.

plainFields.name: phone_number
plainFields.description: Seller's main contact number (SMS/2FA/app notifications). Allows seller-facing service notifications, alerts. Example: '+821099988877'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp for audit, onboarding, lifecycle events. Required for traceability and SLA compliance.

plainFields.name: shop_name
plainFields.description: Shop display title or entity name shown to customers. Implements branding and partner management requirement. Example: 'Seoul Style Socks'.

plainFields.name: deactivated_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion/deactivation timestamp for privacy/compliance lifecycle. Used for logical deletion or account erasure auditability.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_admins
models.description: Admin actor entity - Implements system/admin staff requirements from Role Management. Admins are responsible for platform governance, compliance, and audit. Maintains strict separation of identity, credentials, and assignment of elevated permissions. 3NF compliance is ensured by isolating references and not duplicating data from user_profile. Used for admin login, system event logging, and override actions. Special constraint: All actions must be audit-logged and are subject to multi-factor/secondary verification policies.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for admin entity.

foreignFields.name: user_profile_id
foreignFields.description: Associated user profile's {@link ai_mall_backend_user_profiles.id}. Centralizes admin profile data for compliance, multi-role support, and normalization.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Admin's unique platform login email for authentication/contact. Used for notifications, escalation, and audit linkage. Example: 'admin@mall.com'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Account creation timestamp for audit/compliance slas, etc.

plainFields.name: mfa_enabled
plainFields.description: Multi-factor authentication flag. Implements security policies requiring MFA on admin accounts. Example: true.

plainFields.name: deactivated_at
plainFields.description: Account deactivation or soft deletion timestamp. Used for lifecycle management and compliance.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_ai_agents
models.description: AI Agent actor entity - Implements requirements for internal AI-related service accounts, as per Role and User Management specs. AI agents execute automated operations such as recommendation, moderation, and risk detection. Keeps 3NF via clear separation of secrets, logic, and identity. Example: AI agent handles recommendation delivery with traceable reference to its actions. Key constraint: AI agent roles must be non-impersonable and strictly auditable.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for AI agent service account.

foreignFields.name: user_profile_id
foreignFields.description: Associated user profile's {@link ai_mall_backend_user_profiles.id}. Allows extension, trace, and compliance normalization.

plainFields.name: service_name
plainFields.description: Logical designation of this AI agent (e.g., 'recommender', 'moderator'). Supports programmatic routing and auditing. Example: 'ai_recommendations_worker'.

plainFields.name: enabled
plainFields.description: Whether this AI Agent is active/allowed access. Implements automation workflow control; disables risky AI modules. Example: true.

plainFields.name: last_run_at
plainFields.description: Audit timestamp of last agency activity or automated workflow run. Used for operational monitoring and compliance.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Account/service creation timestamp for traceability and risk tracking.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_user_profiles
models.description: Centralized user profile record - Implements profile normalization and extensibility requirements from the User Management module. Separates PII/contact data, roles, and personalization. Maintains 3NF by keeping profiles normalized and only referenced by actors. Usage: links multi-role identities (customer/seller/admin), supports privacy settings, consent management, and unified notification preferences. Special: Can be extended for new account types or compliance policies.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Surrogate unique identifier for each profile record.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Preferred name or display alias for user. Implements personalization and privacy-friendly addressing. Example: 'Seungmin K.'.

plainFields.name: avatar_url
plainFields.description: Profile avatar image link - used in account UX, personalization, and notifications. Example: 'https://cdn.mall.com/avatar/123.png'.

plainFields.name: consent_marketing
plainFields.description: User's unified consent for marketing communications. Enables privacy control and compliance rights. Example: false.

plainFields.name: locale
plainFields.description: User's preferred locale code (IETF language tag) for UI localization, content, default time zone. Example: 'ko-KR'.

plainFields.name: timezone
plainFields.description: User's preferred IANA timezone ID for notification and scheduling. Example: 'Asia/Seoul'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Profile creation timestamp for auditing and compliance logs.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Profile last update timestamp for synchronization and event logs.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_roles
models.description: Role definition reference - Implements core system role taxonomy as mandated in Roles documentation. Roles distinguish permission boundaries (customer, seller, admin, ai-agent). Normalized; not duplicated in user records. Used for RBAC enforcement, dynamic permission mapping, and auditing. 3NF is enforced by using only role_id foreign key everywhere. Example: Each account is assigned to one or more roles, centrally managed. Special: Adding or removing system roles may extend or restrict platform-wide behaviors.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each role.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Role identifier (slug): 'customer', 'seller', 'admin', 'ai-agent' per platform spec. Implements security and permission boundary. Example: 'customer'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description or system note about this role. For admins, documentation, and audit purpose. Example: 'Customer: can shop and manage own account only.'

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp recorded at role creation for audit, compliance.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_auth_providers
models.description: Authentication provider record - Implements modular extensibility and multi-provider support as required by the User Management module. Providers represent supported login methods (email, oauth, service-token, etc). 3NF compliant; avoids duplication in user/credential tables. Example: 'email_password', 'google', 'kakao', 'service_token'. Special: Adding new providers is possible without schema rewrite. Each credential links to one provider by foreign key, enforcing modularity.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique ID for each supported auth provider.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: Provider type (slug): ENUM: 'email_password', 'social_google', 'social_facebook', 'social_kakao', 'service_token', etc. Value must strictly match app logic and UI. Used for mapping credentials to login flows. Example: 'email_password'.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Provider label or human-friendly display value (UI purposes). Example: 'Google', 'Kakao'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Provider creation timestamp (for auditing, history, and migration).

models.name: ai_mall_backend_credentials
models.description: Authentication credential record - Implements credential storage/assignment to actors via normalization principles (3NF). Each credential is scoped to a single provider (foreign key), and a user actor (customer, seller, admin, ai-agent) by profile/user-specific fields. Password hashes, oauth tokens, or service tokens are stored per security best practices. Credentials may be soft-deleted (revoked) for audit and compliance. Example: Each login method for an account (email, google, service-token) is a separate row. On credential failure/expiry, can be revoked without deleting user. Key: Enforces modular and extensible credentialing without schema rewrite.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for this credential row.

foreignFields.name: auth_provider_id
foreignFields.description: Linked authentication provider's {@link ai_mall_backend_auth_providers.id}. Cleanly separates provider logic from credentialing; critical to modularity and system upgrade.

foreignFields.name: user_profile_id
foreignFields.description: Linked user profile's {@link ai_mall_backend_user_profiles.id}. Ties sensitive credential info to the correct actor. Ensures privacy and audit compliance.

plainFields.name: identifier
plainFields.description: Provider-unique identifier (e.g., email, social ID, service token ID). Must match unique constraint for provider/user combination. Example: 'alice@example.com', 'kakao_oauth_123456'.

plainFields.name: credential_secret
plainFields.description: Stored secret (password hash, OAuth token, service token). Value is hashed/salted/encrypted depending on provider logic. Managed via security policy. Example: '$argon2id$v=19$m=4096,t=3,p=1$...'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Credential creation timestamp, required for audit and compliance with rotation/expiry policies.

plainFields.name: revoked_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for soft deletion/revocation. Present if credential is expired, rotated, or invalidated for cause.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_products
models.description: Product core record - Implements the requirement for product lifecycle and catalog entity from the product management requirements document. Handles all basic product attributes including base title, SKU, status, seller links, pricing method, and configuration. Maintains strict 3NF by putting only atomic product data here. For example, used when a seller creates or updates a product listing. Key relationships: Snapshots for versioning, variants for SKUs, bundles for grouped sales. Special behaviors: Soft-deletion for archiving and audit. No denormalized totals or AI-aggregated data.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each product.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged seller's {@link ai_mall_backend_sellers.id}. Links the product to its owning vendor. Required reference for all products.

plainFields.name: sku
plainFields.description: Product SKU - Implements SKU tracking requirement. Unique seller-assigned code for warehouse and catalog operations. Ensures normalization by placement in core product record only. Example: 'SKU-202508-001'. No nulls allowed.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Main product title - Implements product naming and navigation requirement. Set by the seller or AI enrichment. For example, 'Wireless Headphones Pro'. Required.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Full product description - Allows detailed information for browsing, search, and AI recommendations. Ensures normalization by only including product-level description (detailed variant/content in linked entities). Example: 'Premium noise-cancelling...'. Required.

plainFields.name: price
plainFields.description: Base product price (default variant or minimum) - Atomic monetary value for pricing. For example, 299.0. Not a calculated total, strictly normalized.

plainFields.name: tax_class
plainFields.description: Tax class identifier - Associates correct tax calculation/service in normalized manner. Ensures 3NF.

plainFields.name: inventory_method
plainFields.description: Inventory tracking strategy string. Implements inventory method specification. For example, 'per_variant', 'none', or custom. Keeps normalization by avoiding derived or status fields.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Product status code - e.g. 'active', 'archived', 'pending'. Used for workflow control, archiving, and AI enrichment. No aggregation or denormalization.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Created timestamp - Implements history/audit control. Example: 2025-07-28T07:57:55.559Z. Immutable.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp. Ensures temporal normalization and auditing. Required for business process tracking.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete timestamp. Null if not deleted; used for retention compliance. Normalized deletion, not a status indicator.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_product_snapshots
models.description: Product snapshot records - Implements audit, history, and versioning per snapshot pattern from requirements. Saves all critical product state changes with before/after data, actor, reason, and timestamp. Ensures 3NF by separating history from current product record. Example: Used during product update, AI enrichment, or admin change. Key relationship: Linked to a product; immutable records.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each snapshot.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Source product's {@link ai_mall_backend_products.id}. The product this snapshot version applies to.

foreignFields.name: actor_id
foreignFields.description: Actor's user id responsible for snapshot (customer/admin/seller/ai-agent). Links to user entities in actors namespace (not duplicated).

plainFields.name: snapshot_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for snapshot - Audit and traceability. E.g., 'Price changed by Seller', 'AI auto-enrichment', 'Category change'. Maintains normalization by not embedding product fields here.

plainFields.name: snapshot_data
plainFields.description: Full serialized state of product for audit/version rollback. Typically JSON or binary format. Example: '{"sku":...}'. Not denormalized, but a point-in-time immutable fact. Not a duplicated product field.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Snapshot creation timestamp. Used for version ordering, retention policy, and rollback audit trail. Required.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_variants
models.description: Product variant (option/child SKU) entity - Implements product variant and option design. Each variant represents a unique SKU with its own price, attributes, and inventory linkage. Maintains 3NF by storing only variant-specific atomic data. For example, 'Color: Red, Size: L'. Relates to parent product, inventory, and bundles. Variants are child SKUs, key for multi-option products.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each variant.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Parent product's {@link ai_mall_backend_products.id}. The core product this variant is part of.

plainFields.name: sku
plainFields.description: Variant-specific SKU - Implements accurate warehouse and transaction handling per child SKU. Ensures strict normalization. Example: 'SKU-202508-001-RED-L'. Not null.

plainFields.name: option_values
plainFields.description: JSON-encoded selected option values for this variant (e.g., color/size/material). Maintains 3NF by representing configuration atomically. Example: '{"Color":"Red","Size":"L"}'. Not denormalized; not a reference array.

plainFields.name: price
plainFields.description: Variant price - Atomic monetary value; never a total or derived from bundle/other variants. Strictly normalized. Example: 329.99.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Variant status, e.g., 'active', 'unavailable'. Follows workflow/state transitions and ensures normalization. Not derived/calculated.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Created timestamp (for variant). Used for audit history, not aggregation. Example: 2025-07-28T07:57:55.559Z.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for variant, for audit and rollback. Not derived/calculated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete timestamp (null if active). Allows compliance retention and proper archival. Strictly normalized; not a status field.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_category_products
models.description: Junction table for products-to-categories (M:N) - Implements many-to-many relationship per requirements for flexible product navigation and categorization. Each row links one product to one category, maintaining 3NF. Used when a product needs to be classified under multiple categories or a category contains multiple products. No denormalized/aggregate fields included.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for association row. Unique identifier for each product-category relationship.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Product's {@link ai_mall_backend_products.id} in category.

foreignFields.name: category_id
foreignFields.description: Category's {@link ai_mall_backend_categories.id} this product maps to.

plainFields.name: assigned_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when product was categorized. For audit trail and rollback, not summary/aggregation.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_categories
models.description: Product category reference - Implements flexible, hierarchical category navigation requirement. Allows parent/child category relationships, merchandising metadata, and AI enrichment per requirements. Maintains normalization by only including atomic details. Example: 'Electronics > Headphones'. Key relationships: Products via category_products, parent category (if any). Special behaviors: No denormalized product counts in this entity.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each category.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Self-reference to parent category's {@link ai_mall_backend_categories.id}. Enables multi-level hierarchy. Nullable for root categories.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Unique category code for API reference and integration. Maintains normalization by using code instead of category-derived meanings. Example: 'ELEC-HEADPHONES'.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Category name for UI and navigation. Example: 'Headphones'. Not a denormalized count or string.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Long-form category description for merchant and AI enrichment. Maintains 3NF. Example: 'All headphone products, including wireless and wired.'

plainFields.name: image_uri
plainFields.description: URI to representative image/icon for merchandising. Atomic link field. Example: 'https://cdn.example.com/cat/electronics.jpg'.

plainFields.name: badge
plainFields.description: Optional merchandising badge or icon string. Not used for computed/generative info. Example: 'Best Seller'.

plainFields.name: ranking
plainFields.description: Optional ranking integer for explicit category ordering (not an aggregate count).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Created timestamp for category, used for audit and versioning.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for the category.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-deleted timestamp for category if archived. Null if active. Used for compliance, not as a status field.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_inventory
models.description: Variant-level inventory record - Implements per-variant inventory tracking as required in the product management requirements. Stores atomic count and audit info. Ensures 3NF by not duplicating variant/product data. Example: Each row represents a specific warehouse/location-pool for a variant's inventory state. Relationships: Variant, possible future integration with warehouse/location tables. Behavioral note: No derived or total inventory here; totals calculated in view/materialized only.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each inventory record.

foreignFields.name: variant_id
foreignFields.description: Variant entity's {@link ai_mall_backend_variants.id} this inventory is for.

plainFields.name: quantity_available
plainFields.description: Current available quantity (atomic, not a summary of anything else). Maintains normalization. For example: 35. Required.

plainFields.name: quantity_reserved
plainFields.description: Quantity reserved (committed to carts, not yet shipped). Ensures atomic state, not a calculation.

plainFields.name: quantity_damaged
plainFields.description: Quantity recorded as damaged/unsellable (for audit and compliance). Strict 3NF adherence.

plainFields.name: quantity_backordered
plainFields.description: Quantity on backorder (customer requested higher than stock, not available yet shipped). 3NF: each state recorded, not calculated.

plainFields.name: location
plainFields.description: Warehouse/location code or string for inventory pool. Not a summary field. For example: 'WH-SEOUL-01'.

plainFields.name: audit_reason
plainFields.description: Describes why this record was created/modified (e.g., restock, damage report, inventory adjustment). Maintains audit history and traceability.

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description: User who performed this inventory change. Atomic reference, not duplicated actor data. Null allowed for system-initiated events.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Created timestamp for inventory log.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for the inventory record.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_product_evidence
models.description: Audit evidence for product/version changes - Fulfills requirements for immutable evidence trail and compliance. Directly links to products or snapshots and stores file/media references used as proof for each product update (price, content, etc.). 3NF: Only atomic evidence record per change here. Used in admin approvals, dispute resolution, etc. No aggregate fields. Never stores the media itself, only references.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each evidence record.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Linked product's {@link ai_mall_backend_products.id} if evidence is directly attached (nullable if it's snapshot evidence only).

foreignFields.name: snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: Snapshot's {@link ai_mall_backend_product_snapshots.id} if evidence relates to a specific product snapshot (nullable if evidence on current product only).

foreignFields.name: actor_id
foreignFields.description: User who submitted the evidence (for traceability / responsibility assignment). Null for AI-generated uploads.

plainFields.name: evidence_type
plainFields.description: Type of evidence (image, text, pdf, etc.). Used for filtering and compliance. Not a media blob; only type string.

plainFields.name: evidence_uri
plainFields.description: URI/location of the uploaded evidence. Maintains normalization, never stores data here. Example: 'https://cdn.example.com/evidence/123abc.jpg'. Required.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for evidence submission. Maintains audit trail integrity and submission timing.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_bundles
models.description: Product bundle entity - Implements business requirements for grouping/bundling multiple SKUs as a single sellable entity. Each bundle is a distinct product (for promotion/listing). Details such as bundle title, description, and merchandising are atomic; bundle composition is defined in ai_mall_backend_bundle_products. Normalization ensured by separating actual bundle-product mapping to other table. Bundles can be created/updated by sellers/admins, never derived/calculated.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each bundle.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller who owns/manages the bundle. Reference to {@link ai_mall_backend_sellers.id}. Required link; not duplicated data.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Unique bundle code for programmatic reference, tracking, and integrations. Example: 'BUNDLE-ELX-202507'. Not null, prevents confusion/manipulation. Maintains 3NF.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Bundle title shown to customers. For example: 'Ultimate Gaming Headphone Set'. Strictly atomic for normalized navigation/catalog.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Full long-form description for promotion, compliance, and customer info. Not denormalized summaries. Example: 'Includes Headphone Pro + Pouch + Warranty Extension'.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Bundle status/workflow indicator (e.g., 'active', 'archived'). Required per business regulation. No aggregation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Bundle creation timestamp. Maintains full audit trail for bundle lifecycle and regulatory retention.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last change timestamp for bundle.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-deletion timestamp if archived. Maintains compliance, not a denormalized status.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_bundle_products
models.description: Bundle-variant junction entity - Implements normalized M:N relationship between bundles and product variants as required for bundled sales. Each row connects one bundle to one variant SKU, specifying the quantity of that SKU in the bundle. Ensures 3NF by not duplicating variant or bundle data. No derived totals - only atomic mapping. Examples: Used to ensure correct bundle composition at checkout or for bundle price adjustment rules.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each bundle-variant mapping row.

foreignFields.name: bundle_id
foreignFields.description: Bundle's {@link ai_mall_backend_bundles.id}.

foreignFields.name: variant_id
foreignFields.description: Variant's {@link ai_mall_backend_variants.id} included in this bundle.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Quantity of this variant included in the bundle. For example: 2 for '2 x Headphones'. Strictly atomic field, not a derived/cached sum.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_product_media
models.description: Product media record - Implements image/media enrichment, localization, and AI-assistable content by providing atomic records for each image/video/asset attached to a product or variant. Maintains 3NF by never duplicating the asset data; only holding references. Example: Stores media URI, type (image/video), and which product/variant it attaches to. No calculated/AI-summarized data here. Used for catalog navigation, customer UI, and compliance audit.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each product media asset.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Product's {@link ai_mall_backend_products.id} this media belongs to. Can be null if this media is attached to a variant only.

foreignFields.name: variant_id
foreignFields.description: Variant's {@link ai_mall_backend_variants.id} this media is associated with. Can be null for product-level images.

plainFields.name: media_type
plainFields.description: Type of media (image, video, 3d, etc). Normalized atomic string type for UI and analytics. Example: 'image'.

plainFields.name: media_uri
plainFields.description: URI of the media asset, e.g., 'https://cdn.example.com/images/prod-1234.jpg'. Strictly reference only, not the media data.

plainFields.name: locale
plainFields.description: Optional localization/variant - BCP 47 locale code or null for default. Enables multilingual assets without denormalizing product/variant itself. Example: 'en-US', 'ko-KR'.

plainFields.name: alt_text
plainFields.description: Optional alt-text/caption for accessibility and SEO. Strictly atomic text field, not derived from product info.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when media was attached, for compliance and UI refresh tracking.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_carts
models.description: Cart - Implements the cart entity required for multi-channel, tenant-aware, user-specific shopping cart management with full audit trail, session/channel separation, and soft-deletion support. This is in strict 3NF; all pre-calculated data is excluded. All attributes and relationships adhere to the business and normalization requirements outlined in the order fulfillment (04_ai-mall-backend_order-fulfillment.md) and audit logging modules.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for a cart.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_backend_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link ai_mall_backend_customers.id}. Associates a cart with its owner for all customer-specific operations and analytics.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_backend_channel_id
foreignFields.description: Channel context's {@link ai_mall_backend_channels.id}. Associates each cart with a particular channel for proper segregation and fulfillment routing.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp cart was created, for lifecycle and audit tracking.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for most recent update to the cart, for change history and business process compliance.

plainFields.name: abandoned_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when cart was marked as abandoned. Null if not abandoned; used for journey analytics and retention workflows.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Null if active; required for retention, auditability, and compliance purposes.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_cart_items
models.description: Cart Item - Each itemized record in the cart tied to a specific product, variant, and/or bundle. Strict 3NF compliance—no calculated fields, all pricing/summary data is deferred to order calculation or materialized views. Required for traceable, atomic management of shopping cart contents with soft-deletion for abandoned/recovered cart item handling.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for a cart item record.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_backend_cart_id
foreignFields.description: Parent cart's {@link ai_mall_backend_carts.id}. Enables grouping all items by cart for order/batch actions.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_backend_product_id
foreignFields.description: Product's {@link ai_mall_backend_products.id}. Foreign key for analytics and item validation. Required for every cart item.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_backend_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Variant's {@link ai_mall_backend_variants.id} (nullable for non-variant items). Enables option/variant-level granularity; null if not a variant SKU.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_backend_bundle_id
foreignFields.description: If the item is part of a bundle: {@link ai_mall_backend_bundles.id} (nullable). Supports per-bundle itemization; null otherwise.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Atomically tracked number of units for this item in the cart. Direct input, strictly atomic, not a calculated value.

plainFields.name: added_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp this item was added, for audit and analytics.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for this item.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp, supporting recovery/auditing of cart items. Null if active.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_cart_snapshots
models.description: Cart Snapshot - Temporal/audit entity for history and analytics of cart state transitions. Strictly normalized; stores event, state-as-JSON, and timestamp with reference to the source cart. Read-only/append-only log for full auditability and evidence in compliance, rollback, and analytics scenarios.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for this snapshot event.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_backend_cart_id
foreignFields.description: Source cart's {@link ai_mall_backend_carts.id} for this snapshot. Maintains full referential history for all state transitions.

plainFields.name: snapshot_event
plainFields.description: Event label that triggered the snapshot (e.g., 'checked_out', 'abandoned', 'item_added'). Atomic, required string representing the action.

plainFields.name: cart_state_json
plainFields.description: JSON-serialized representation of the cart state at the event. Required for rollback and full evidence audit; string for maximum compatibility.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cart snapshot was recorded. Audit and compliance requirement.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_orders
models.description: Order Entity - Implements core transactional order requirement as per Order Fulfillment & Payments doc. This model captures the complete atomic record for each commercial purchase, including customer linkage and lifecycle status. Compliance with 3NF: all aggregate data handled elsewhere, only atomic fields in this model. Example: Represents a customer's single purchase, splitting by seller if required.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique order identifier.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link ai_mall_backend_customers.id}. Each order tracks its customer for access and audit.

plainFields.name: order_number
plainFields.description: Business visible tracking code; unique identifier for user-facing order lookup. Ensures traceability; unique-indexed.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Order status at this state (pending, confirmed, paid, fulfilled, shipped, delivered, cancelled, etc). Atomic (not computed).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for order creation, for audit trail and workflow.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last order record update. Supports audit logging and temporal queries.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete field for retention policies. Null if active.

plainFields.name: note
plainFields.description: Optional note/comment from customer for order. Atomic data only.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_order_items
models.description: Order Item - Captures each individual product/variant included in an order, per line, according to Order Fulfillment requirements. Strictly normalized: stores item, product, and unit price at the time of purchase. Multivendor support: links to seller. Each record immutable beyond cancellation/returns. Example: An order for two products, each with a variant, will have two associated records here.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each order line item.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Parent order's {@link ai_mall_backend_orders.id}. Associates line item to order.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Product's {@link ai_mall_backend_products.id}. What was sold (cross-reference for normalization).

foreignFields.name: variant_id
foreignFields.description: Variant's {@link ai_mall_backend_variants.id}. SKU-level specifics (size, color etc), nullable for base products.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Quantity of this SKU for this order line. Normalized: totals/calculations done externally.

plainFields.name: price
plainFields.description: Unit price at purchase (historically tracked here, no aggregation).

plainFields.name: seller_id
plainFields.description: Belonged seller's {@link ai_mall_backend_sellers.id}. References who fulfills this line item.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Product name at time of order (snapshot, not FK). For past accuracy even after catalog/title changes.

plainFields.name: note
plainFields.description: Optional per-item customer note (gift messages etc).

models.name: ai_mall_backend_order_status_logs
models.description: Order Status Log - Implements full immutable status trail of each order lifecycle transition (required for audit/compliance). Each entry captures a discrete state change, with actor and optionally reason/code. 3NF: Only atomic data, no aggregates.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique for each status log record.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Linked order's {@link ai_mall_backend_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: actor_id
foreignFields.description: Actor's {@link ai_mall_backend_roles.id}. Refers to who triggered the change (customer, seller, admin, ai-agent).

plainFields.name: from_status
plainFields.description: Status before the transition. Workflow audit detail.

plainFields.name: to_status
plainFields.description: Status after the transition (to what state).

plainFields.name: changed_at
plainFields.description: When this change occurred.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Optional business/automation reason for the transition.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_shipments
models.description: Shipment Entity - Holds each shipment/fulfillment event related to orders. Records atomic carrier, status, tracking. No aggregates. Key for split fulfillment, multi-shipment and auditability. Contains address as atomic snapshot field (not FK).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique shipping record.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Order's {@link ai_mall_backend_orders.id}. Which order is being fulfilled.

plainFields.name: tracking_number
plainFields.description: Tracking code from shipping provider. May be null for orders not yet shipped or pick-up.

plainFields.name: carrier
plainFields.description: Carrier or shipping partner (e.g., UPS, FedEx).

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Shipment/delivery state e.g. pending, shipped, delivered, returned. Atomic step only.

plainFields.name: address
plainFields.description: Frozen snapshot of destination address at time of shipment event (per audit/compliance) not a reference.

plainFields.name: shipped_at
plainFields.description: Date/time shipped (if applicable, null if not shipped yet).

plainFields.name: delivered_at
plainFields.description: Date/time delivered (if applicable, null if not).

models.name: ai_mall_backend_payments
models.description: Payment Entity - One payment record per payment event towards an order, may be split for mixed method or partial payments. Atomic: Amount, method, status, transaction. Never aggregates. Serves as both audit log and for reconciliation. Example: Split payments generate two records for same order.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Payment record identifier.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Order's {@link ai_mall_backend_orders.id}. Relation to order paid for.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Paying customer's {@link ai_mall_backend_customers.id}. Who initiated payment.

plainFields.name: method
plainFields.description: Payment type (e.g., card, wallet, points, bank transfer).

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: Atomic amount for this payment. Calculations (totals) not stored here.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Payment status (pending, completed, failed, refunded).

plainFields.name: transaction_id
plainFields.description: ID from external payment processor (auditable reference for PCI), may be null if not yet available.

plainFields.name: approved_at
plainFields.description: Date/time payment approved (if completed).

plainFields.name: cancelled_at
plainFields.description: When payment was cancelled/refunded if so.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_order_snapshots
models.description: Order Snapshot Entity - Captures immutable, point-in-time JSON (string) representations of the entire order state at key lifecycle events (creation, update, cancel). Pure audit trail: never updated, only appended. Relationship: tracks which order and what actor/system captured the snapshot.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for snapshot record.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Snapshotted order's {@link ai_mall_backend_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: actor_id
foreignFields.description: Actor who triggered the snapshot. {@link ai_mall_backend_roles.id}.

plainFields.name: snapshot_reason
plainFields.description: Reason/context of snapshot (creation, modification, system event, etc). Atomic context data.

plainFields.name: snapshot_data
plainFields.description: Serialized representation of order at this point. Only atomic string/JSON, no computation here.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When snapshot recorded. Temporal audit/compliance.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_coupons
models.description: Coupon Master Table - Implements the foundational coupon definition requirement from Promotions & Loyalty. Centralized store for coupon type definitions with code, discount, rules, period and linkage to campaigns. Maintains separation from per-actor issuance (3NF), used for campaign reporting, auditing, and analytics.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique Coupon identifier for the definition itself.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_backend_campaign_id
foreignFields.description: Linked Campaign's {@link ai_mall_backend_campaigns.id}. Connects this coupon to an optional campaign. Null if no campaign linkage.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Coupon code - unique presentation for users to redeem, e.g., SPRING20. Enforces system uniqueness for no conflicts.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Coupon display name shown to users.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed user-facing description, terms and legal notes for the coupon.

plainFields.name: discount_type
plainFields.description: Discount type: 'percentage', 'fixed', 'freeship', etc. (enum supported at logic level).

plainFields.name: discount_value
plainFields.description: Stored discount value, interpreted per discount_type field. Atomic value, never a calculation result.

plainFields.name: minimum_spend
plainFields.description: Minimum required spend for use of coupon to be eligible.

plainFields.name: valid_from
plainFields.description: Start date/time of coupon validity window.

plainFields.name: valid_until
plainFields.description: End date/time of coupon validity window.

plainFields.name: max_uses_per_user
plainFields.description: Maximum allowed redemptions per user.

plainFields.name: total_redemption_limit
plainFields.description: Total redemption cap for coupon across all users.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether coupon is currently enabled/allowed for issuance/redemption.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Row creation timestamp for audit.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Row update timestamp for audit.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_campaigns
models.description: Promotion campaign grouping table – for tracking and configuring campaigns that group or schedule one or more coupons. Supports reporting, enable/disable flows, and campaign-wide rules.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique Campaign identifier.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Campaign name for analytics and reporting, e.g. 'Holiday2025'. Unique in scope.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional campaign documentation.

plainFields.name: starts_at
plainFields.description: Campaign validity start datetime.

plainFields.name: ends_at
plainFields.description: Campaign validity end datetime.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether campaign is currently enabled or paused systemwide.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Audit: campaign created at timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Audit: last update to campaign.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_coupon_issuances
models.description: Coupon Issuance Ledger – assignment record of a coupon to a specific actor (customer, seller, etc.). Ensures traceability for compliance and anti-abuse monitoring. Maintains atomicity: no mixing of issuance and definition data.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique ID for the issuance event.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_backend_coupon_id
foreignFields.description: Coupon reference {@link ai_mall_backend_coupons.id}. FK to coupon master table.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_backend_campaign_id
foreignFields.description: Campaign reference {@link ai_mall_backend_campaigns.id}. For campaign-tracked issuances; nullable for ad-hoc issuance.

foreignFields.name: actor_id
foreignFields.description: Recipient actor (customer, seller, etc.) – FK to Actors schema; polymorphic lookup.

plainFields.name: issued_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this coupon was issued to actor.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Explicit expiry for this issuance (per personalization or campaign rule).

plainFields.name: issued_by
plainFields.description: FK to the issuer (admin/seller/AI) who assigned the coupon.

plainFields.name: is_redeemed
plainFields.description: Flag for whether coupon has been fully redeemed/used.

plainFields.name: redeemed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of redemption, nullable if not yet used.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_coupon_usages
models.description: Coupon Usage Event Ledger – granular record of each coupon use (redemption), auditability and fraud detection. Each row maps to specific coupon issuance, actor, and order (via Orders schema).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique usage event identifier.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_backend_coupon_issuance_id
foreignFields.description: FK to coupon issuance ({@link ai_mall_backend_coupon_issuances.id}).

foreignFields.name: actor_id
foreignFields.description: Redeemer (actor/user) – Actor schema FK.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Order FK {@link ai_mall_backend_orders.id} (from Orders schema).

plainFields.name: discount_applied

models.name: ai_mall_backend_loyalty_points
models.description: Loyalty Points Program Master Ledger – one row per unique point program (e.g., storewide points, VIP miles), referenced for ledgers/usage. Centralizes conversion, expiration, rates, and program logic.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each point program.

plainFields.name: program_name
plainFields.description: Unique business label for program (e.g., 'Mall Points').

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Program documentation/detail.

plainFields.name: accrual_rate
plainFields.description: Number of points earned per currency unit spent.

plainFields.name: redemption_rate
plainFields.description: Currency value per point (conversion rate).

plainFields.name: expiration_days
plainFields.description: Days after accrual when points expire, nullable for never-expire.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Program status flag (active/inactive).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Program creation timestamp for audit/history.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Program update timestamp.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_loyalty_point_ledgers
models.description: Point Ledger Table – tracks accrual, deduction, and adjustment of points per actor per program. Serves for balance calculation, compliance, and audit trail. Each row is an atomic transaction.

primaryField.name: id

foreignFields.name: loyalty_point_program_id
foreignFields.description: FK to program ({@link ai_mall_backend_loyalty_points.id}).

foreignFields.name: actor_id
foreignFields.description: FK to actor (customer/seller/admin), from Actors schema.

plainFields.name: transaction_type
plainFields.description: Transaction type: 'accrual', 'deduction', 'adjustment', etc.

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: Positive = points credited; negative = debited.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Narrative for audit/explanation.

plainFields.name: related_order_id
plainFields.description: FK to order (nullable – points may not always be tied to an order).

plainFields.description: Event timestamp for the point action.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_point_usages

primaryField.name: id

foreignFields.name: loyalty_point_ledger_id
foreignFields.description: FK to point ledger ({@link ai_mall_backend_loyalty_point_ledgers.id}) from which points are debited.

foreignFields.description: FK to actor (redeemer, e.g., customer/seller), from Actors schema.

plainFields.name: used_at

models.name: ai_mall_backend_inquiries
models.description: Inquiry Master Record - Implements the end-to-end requirements for structured customer/seller/platform communications (e.g., Q&A, support, feedback) as described in the business requirements. Maintains strict 3NF normalization (threads and attachments are separated into relevant tables). Typically used for a customer's inquiry regarding an order or product, links to actor (customer/seller), and can reference product/order as context. Key relationships: references actors (customers, sellers, admins) in other domains; parent to ai_mall_backend_inquiry_threads and ai_mall_backend_inquiry_attachments. primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique inquiry identifier for audit and retrieval.

foreignFields.description: Polymorphic reference to actor who created the inquiry (customer, seller, or admin). Refers to the UUID in the actor table relevant to the inquiry type. No direct Prisma relation due to cross-domain FK - enforce and resolve in app logic.

foreignFields.name: related_product_id
foreignFields.description: Optional related product's {@link ai_mall_backend_products.id}. For inquiries tied to a product.

foreignFields.name: related_order_id
foreignFields.description: Optional related order's {@link ai_mall_backend_orders.id}. For inquiries tied to an order.

plainFields.name: inquiry_type
plainFields.description: Atomic string for type: e.g., 'product_question', 'order_issue', 'platform_feedback'. Maintains 3NF normalization.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: String indicating open/pending/closed/escalated/resolved. Lifecycle traceability.

plainFields.name: subject
plainFields.description: Short title/subject of the inquiry. Example: 'Delayed shipment inquiry'. Used for listing/searching.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp; traceability and ordering.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Update timestamp for content/status changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-deletion timestamp; null if active. For regulatory compliance.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_inquiry_threads
models.description: Inquiry Message Thread - Provides normalized conversation history per inquiry as required by the Q&A/message board model in the business requirements. Each row is a message/follow-up within an inquiry, from a customer, seller, admin, or system. Key relationships: linked to ai_mall_backend_inquiries (required) and the actor that submitted the thread. Attachments reference this via ai_mall_backend_inquiry_attachments. Ensures 3NF and separation of message content.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique thread message identifier.

foreignFields.name: inquiry_id
foreignFields.description: Parent inquiry's {@link ai_mall_backend_inquiries.id}. Required for every thread message.

foreignFields.name: actor_id
foreignFields.description: Polymorphic reference to actor (customer, seller, or admin) who submitted the message. Refers to actor UUID; enforce in application logic. No direct Prisma relation due to actor polymorphic nature.

plainFields.name: message
plainFields.description: Body/content of the thread message. Large text or system message.

plainFields.name: message_type

models.name: ai_mall_backend_audit_logs
models.description: System-wide audit log for tracking sensitive or high-value actions and changes, as required by security and compliance requirements from the Architecture, Security, and Compliance documents. This table implements the evidence and immutability protocols, providing an authoritative record of who did what and when. Maintains full 3NF normalization by isolating audit records from business and transaction data. For example, every privileged API call, admin action, or automated AI-triggered event inserts one row, preserving actor, action, and context. Key relationships: May reference actors or affected entities (from other schemas) but contains only logging context. Special behaviors: Should be append-only for audit integrity.

plainFields.name: target_table

plainFields.name: target_id

plainFields.name: details
plainFields.description: Human-readable or structured JSON description of the event for investigation purposes. Ensures no non-atomic data is stored (free text, not aggregated). For example: 'Changed pricing rule X'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the log entry was created. Implements immutable evidence requirement; supports temporal queries and compliance reporting.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_event_logs
models.description: Asynchronous, append-only event log for system-level or cross-domain events. Implements the event-driven architecture objective from the Architecture & Extensibility spec—captures all significant business events (e.g., order placed, stock updated, review posted) for use by bus consumers, integrations, and microservices. Maintains normalization by storing only atomic event metadata and business context, never duplicating data from source tables. Usage examples: inserts align with system triggers; consumers process events according to type and payload. Key relationships: no direct foreign keys, as source models reside in other schemas. Special behaviors: typically read-only except for system writes; can be purged according to retention policy.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique event log sequence; provides idempotency and cross-system traceability.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Event type code (e.g., 'order_placed', 'inventory_updated', 'user_banned'). Implements contract for event consumers/handlers. Strictly atomic, never pre-calculated.

plainFields.name: event_payload
plainFields.description: JSON or serialized string containing event parameters (business-context details). Provides contract for event consumers to process payload. Never denormalized; event context only.

plainFields.name: raised_by_id
plainFields.description: ID for the actor (system, admin, or AI-agent) that emitted the event. Supports auditability and access control workflows. Can be null for pure system events.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of event emission. Ensures sequenced, temporal event analytics and replay in architecture modules.

models.name: ai_mall_backend_integration_keys

plainFields.description: Timestamp when key was issued/enabled. Used for rotation, expiration, and audit queries. Never derived or pre-calculated.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: (Optional) expiry of the integration key for forced rotation. Maintains access hygiene. Null if perpetual/managed externally.

### `ai_mall_backend_channels`

Channel Entity - Implements the requirement for a unified platform channel registry as described in the architecture documentation. This table manages the definition and configuration of each business channel (web, mobile, partner integration, etc.), ensuring systematic onboarding, channel identity, routing controls, and auditability. Strict 3NF normalization—channel-specific settings and runtime data are separated into auxiliary tables to avoid redundancy. For example, creating an entry for a new branded web UI or a mobile app channel. Key relationships: sections, tenants, and API gateways reference this for channel-scoped logic. Special behaviors: Channels may be dynamically enabled/disabled, must be unique by code.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `tenant_id`: Associated tenant's [ai_mall_backend_tenants.id](#ai_mall_backend_tenants). Ensures that each channel is scoped to a valid tenant/brand context, enforcing strict multi-tenancy.
- `code`: Channel code (slug or short name) - Implements the unique identity requirement. Used for routing and lookup, e.g., "web", "mobile", "partner1". Enforces normalization by not storing display names or configs redundantly.
- `name`: Human-readable channel name - For admin/business reference. For example, "Mobile App Channel (2025)", ensures normalized separation from settings or localized values.
- `enabled`: Activation flag - Implements the requirement for dynamic channel enable/disable. Ensures business logic only routes traffic for enabled channels.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp - Implements audibility. Example: "2025-07-28T16:57:55+09:00". Never null; used in logs.
- `updated_at`: Last modification timestamp. Used for sync and audit trails, not null. Updated on any change.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp - For retention/audit. If not null, channel is considered deleted. Satisfies compliance requirement for data retention/auditability.

### `ai_mall_backend_sections`

Section Entity - Implements extensible, dynamic business section management, mapping to a requirement for modular dynamic site/app composition. Each entry defines a logical section/component within a given channel context (e.g., home banner, product carousel, promo area). Maintains strict 3NF by referencing both channels and storing only section configuration here; layout/data references in auxiliary tables/materialized views if needed. Example: onboarding an app 'Main Banner' section for 'mobile' channel. Key relationships: references ai_mall_backend_channels; may be referenced by content/config tables elsewhere. Special behaviors: Can be dynamically enabled/disabled or scheduled, but schedules are not stored here.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `channel_id`: Related channel's [ai_mall_backend_channels.id](#ai_mall_backend_channels); identifies which channel this section belongs to, ensuring no cross-channel confusion.
- `code`: Section code (domain-unique slug) - Used for programmatic reference. E.g., "main_banner", "featured_products". Meets normalization requirement: display name, config are not duplicated here.
- `name`: Display name for the section (for admin/UIs), e.g., "Main Banner". Atomic, not null. Used for search/UI, separated from configuration content.
- `enabled`: Logical activation flag for business scheduling. Required by dynamic rendering rules for channel UX composition. Must remain atomic; scheduling logic is externalized.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for the section. Implements audit trail requirement. Not null.
- `updated_at`: Change timestamp; always updated on row update. Not null. Used in auxiliary processing and audit logging.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-deletion timestamp; null if not deleted, value set when removed for audit/compliance. Enforces audit/history policy.

### `ai_mall_backend_configurations`

Configuration Entity - Satisfies the requirements for a centralized configuration registry (feature toggles, branded settings, etc.). Each row specifies a single atomic configuration item, maintaining 3NF and not duplicating setting values. For instance, feature toggles, limits, branding variables, API keys (encrypted elsewhere). Relationships: references channel and optional section for scope; config values are always atomic. Usage example: enabling a feature in a specific section of the web channel. Special behaviors: Only stores atomic key-value data. Aggregates or computed/pre-resolved settings are handled in views/external caches.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `channel_id`: Configured channel's [ai_mall_backend_channels.id](#ai_mall_backend_channels). Null if config is system-global. Maintains 2NF: channel-specific overrides do not duplicate global config data.
- `section_id`: Configured section's [ai_mall_backend_sections.id](#ai_mall_backend_sections). Null if config is for entire channel.
- `name`: Config item name (machine-readable); enforced unique within channel/section scope. Normalized; avoids redundancy vs. human description. E.g., "max_recommended_items", "brand_accent_color".
- `value`: Config value (atomic). Storing as string makes it flexible for all config types. Atomic value by design—complex/aggregated representations handled outside core table. Example: "10", "#F47623", or JSON-encoded value. Enforces normalization: no multi-setting/storage.
- `description`: Description or business comment - For admin clarity and auditability. For example, "Controls max items on home banner". Not used in production logic, only as meta.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp - Satisfies audit/logging and change traceability.
- `updated_at`: Modification timestamp; updated on any change. Implements audit trail requirement; not null.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-deletion timestamp, null if still active. Enforces compliance/audit/max retention. Satisfies business policy for configuration sunset/reversion.

### `ai_mall_backend_api_gateways`

API Gateway Entity - Implements registry of API gateway endpoints, configs, and associations (see Architecture requirements for API gateway concept). Each record defines an API endpoint, domain mapping, and metadata for routing/auth. Strict normalization—one entry per gateway/route, no calculated fields. For example, registering "api.mall.com/v2" as the main API route for the 'web' channel. Key relationships: references channel (for business context); referenced by tenant or system audit if required. Special behaviors: Gateway can be temporarily suspended/enabled, and settings beyond route are handled externally.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `channel_id`: Target channel's [ai_mall_backend_channels.id](#ai_mall_backend_channels); ensures requests are mapped to the correct business context.
- `route_base`: Base route for this gateway (e.g., "/api/v1", "/mobile/"). Implements requirement for explicit, unambiguous routing. Atomic. No computed path fields stored here.
- `domain`: Mapped domain for this gateway (FQDN or subdomain, e.g., "api.mall.com"). Per domain mapping, not null. No wildcard; each gateway registered separately. Used in endpoint discovery.
- `enabled`: Gateway activation flag—allows quick suspension/reactivation. Only unaggregated atomic flag here.
- `created_at`: Gateway creation time (audit/logs).
- `updated_at`: Last config update timestamp (audit/tracking). Always required per system audit rules.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-delete timestamp if gateway route is removed. Null means active. Complies with retention, audit policies.

### `ai_mall_backend_tenants`

Tenant Entity - Implements the business requirement for full multi-tenancy isolation, as described in system architecture and compliance documents. Each row defines a distinct brand, sub-platform, or logical business tenant (e.g., for white-labeling, brand separation, regional variants). Design: strictly 3NF; all channel, user, and config references use tenant_id rather than duplicating brand/business info. For example, onboarding a new brand/partner, all data is tied to a unique tenant. Key relationships: referenced by channels, users, configurations, etc. Special behaviors: Tenant may be archived, not deleted, to maintain historical integrity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `code`: Tenant code (unique per instance) - e.g., "main_mall", "brandA", "partner2". Used for programmatic routing and scoping. Normalized: display name/config not duplicated here.
- `name`: Display/business name of tenant (for admin/partner reference). Not null, atomic, normalized.
- `archived`: Tenant archival flag—used for compliance, never hard-deletes. Implements regulatory retention. Example: true if tenant/brand offboarded.
- `created_at`: When this tenant/brand was onboarded. Used for onboarding processes, billing, audit.
- `updated_at`: Last updated time; always atomic, not null, per audit policy.
